channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: 25 Years After 9/11, Trump Personifies a Nation Moving On
item.description: The president has de-emphasized and shifted the war on terrorism at a time when fear of foreign attack has receded into the background of American life.

item.title: NPR: The voices of Sept. 11: 'My first thought was ... I can't believe that I survived'
item.description: We listen back to interviews recorded in the aftermath of Sept. 11, with a particular focus on stories of survival and loss at the World Trade Center, and some reflections in poetry and music.

item.title: BBC News: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons
item.description: The revelations in Anthropic's threat intelligence report come after a former top researcher at the company warned of the risks of AI to humanity.

item.title: The Guardian: Curse of the Nile’s gold: how Sudan is losing its fertile fields and ability to produce food
item.description: An artisanal mining boom driven by war and poverty is causing a public health emergency, as chemicals poison soil, water and society In Abu Hamad, on the banks of the Nile, verdant orchards, gardens and fields once produ…

item.title: Al Jazeera: The vanishing pharmacy of the Sundarbans
item.description: As rising seas push salt into the world's largest mangrove, traditional medicinal plants are being lost.

item.title: Ars Technica: Claude users found ways around safeguards for bioweapons research
item.description: Some dangerous biology looks much like legitimate research, complicating AI safeguards.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: How 9/11 Made Everyone a Conspiracy Theorist
item.description: Crackpot theories were once the stuff of shortwave radio, but September 11 unleashed the Age of Alex Jones.

item.title: WIRED Science: August 2026 Was the Hottest Month Ever Recorded: Copernicus Data
item.description: While the strengthening El Niño helped boost temperatures, climate change is the main culprit for making August so hot.

item.title: WIRED Business: Why So Many AI Researchers Think the Machines Could Kill Everyone
item.description: A combination of rapid advances, recursive self-improvement, and agentic swarms are genuinely “spooking people” inside big labs.

item.title: The New Yorker: The U.S. Was Never Going to Win the “War on Terror”
item.description: In the twenty-five years since 9/11, the U.S. has waged several military campaigns against extremism around the world, resulting in the deaths of almost a million people. What has it accomplished?

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: The Woman Hooking Up Despite Her Body Insecurity
item.description: In this week’s story, a copywriter goes on dates and tries to be less hard on herself.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: The Last NIMBY in a YIMBY Town
item.description: Andrew Berman’s crusade to preserve the West Village has put him at odds with just about everyone.

item.title: Fox59: 19-year-old shot to death in back of an Uber on Indy's far east side
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS -- A 19-year-old man is dead following a shooting along Mitthoefer Road on Indy’s far east side Wednesday night. Police are still investigating exactly what led to the deadly shooting, which took place after…

item.title: Mirror Indy: Here’s who’s running for school board in Beech Grove
item.description: These three candidates will run unopposed to keep their seats. The post Here’s who’s running for school board in Beech Grove appeared first on Mirror Indy .
